title: Embargo Windows, Release-Notes Aggregation & Phased Performance Gates for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context:
We need a single, repeatable release-train pattern that coordinates three product surfaces (Redwood API, Redwood Console, serving Runtime) across regional embargo windows, automated release-note aggregation, and phased rollout gates driven by runtime canary metrics. Current launches are manual, error-prone, and cause late-breaking scope decisions that cascade to docs and GTM.

Goals:
- Define milestone cadence and explicit scope-lock moments for each lane (API, Console, Runtime) that align with legal/region embargoes.
- Implement an automated release-notes pipeline that pulls PR titles/descriptions, Confluence change summaries, and changelog snippets into a single draft artifact for stakeholder review.
- Create phased release gates (canary -> limited -> broad) with clear quantitative pass/fail signals from the runtime (latency P50/P95, error-rate, token throughput) and Console health checks.
- Surface all dependency signals (infra features, dedicated capacity availability, security review) into the release decision dashboard.

Scope in/out:
In-scope: milestone calendar, scope-lock rules, release-note aggregation format and governance, canary metric set and threshold recommendations, embargo window templates, runbook for rollback and hotfix, integration hooks for GH/Confluence/Datadog dashboards.
Out-of-scope: implementation of multi-region infra; detailed infra allocations (will be coordinated with ENG).

Deliverables:
- Milestone calendar with hard scope-lock dates and fallbacks per region.
- Release-note aggregation script + Confluence template + draft approval workflow.
- Canary metric checklist and automated gating config (probe queries + expected thresholds).
- Runbook for phased rollouts and rollback decision tree.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Milestone calendar accepted by PM, Eng leads, and Design.
- Release-notes aggregation produces a draft with at least 80% automation (PRs + Confluence + manual notes) and email/button to request review.
- Canary gate emits pass/fail and ties to rollout automation (stop/pause on failure).
- Embargo templates exist for NA/EU/APAC with comms checklist and legal signoff path.

Notes and constraints:
- Some runtime SLOs are still being finalized (see ENG-5240) — we will draft conservative thresholds and iterate.
- Security review may be required for any change touching telemetry pipelines (security_review_required=true).

comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff with Eng leads + Design. Agreed milestone cadence = 6-week train with a 72h scope-lock for API/Console and 96h for Runtime (longer due to model rollout verification). Action: Owen to draft calendar.

2025-02-19 - Owen Martinez: Posted initial milestone calendar in Confluence and linked dependency matrix. Noted two infra blockers: capacity for Dedicated canary and updated KV-cache hooks (ENG-7012, ENG-7013).
2025-02-24 - Riley Chen (Design): Reviewed release-note template. Recommended separating 'user-facing changes' vs 'developer-impacting' sections. Will provide copy examples by 2025-02-28.

2025-03-01 - Eng Lead (Marco Silva): Scoped canary metric list. Proposed primary checks: token-per-second stability, P95 latency < target_tier, error-rate < 0.2%. We flagged ENG-5240 dependency for telemetry schema.
notes: Decision trade-offs: We intentionally keep the Runtime scope-lock window longer to allow for end-to-end model and kernel compatibility checks. Risk: longer freeze increases pressure on API/Console patches; mitigation: add a fast-path emergency patch process with explicit rollback windows.
